To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
collagen 1 promotes BC cell survival through DDR1-dependent Kv10.1 over-expression, and that this is accompanied by Orai1 expression, co-localization and Ca2+ influx.
collagen 1 promotes survival in human BC cells through the upregulation of Kv10.10 and Orai1 ion channels, through DDR1-dependent ERK1/ERK2 pathway.
the collagen type 1/DDR-1 pathway induces BC cell survival through the activation of the Kv10. 1/Orai1 ion channels and their interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the tumor microenvironment on breast cancer progression.
the identification of new targets for the development of anti-cancer drugs.
a new pathway that regulates BC cell survival and could represent a potential target for BC therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
collagen 1 promotes BC cell survival through the activation of DDR1/ERK1/2 pathway that leads to Kv10.1 overexpression and the consequent increase in Orai1 expression and activity.
the collagen type 1/DDR 1 pathway induces BC cell survival through the overexpression of Orai1 and Kv10.1 channels.
collagen 1 promotes survival and ERK1/ 2 activation in BC cells by increasing Kv10.1, Orai1 and their co-localization on the plasma membrane through DDR1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the survival of breast cancer cells growing in collagen 1 coating is mediated by Kv10.1, which is overexpressed and activated in response to collagen 1 through a mechanism involving DDR1.
collagen 1 promotes survival through DDR1-dependent activation of Kv10. 1 and Orai 1 channels, which in turn increase Ca2+ influx, ERK1-2 phosphorylation and cell survival.
the interaction between collagen type I and DDR1 induces the activation of Kv10. 1/Orai 1 complex that promotes the survival of BC cells by ERK1/ 2 phosphorylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Kv10.1 is an important player in BC cell survival, and this is mediated by a collagen 1/ERK1/2-dependent signaling.
the Kv10/1-Orai1 complex represents a checkpoint of tumor cell survival in the tumor microenvironment, and that this is dependent on DDR1.
Kv10.1, Orai1 and DDR1 are involved in the survival of breast cancer cells.
